qualitative.gate_2_reason: Discretionary big-ticket capital purchases (business jets, specialized vehicles) deferrable in recessions.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Rejected – G2 Essential Need). Textron is heavily exposed to cyclical and discretionary big-ticket corporate and consumer purchases through its Textron Aviation segment (Cessna Citation business jets, Beechcraft turboprops) and Industrial segment (E-Z-GO golf carts, specialized commercial vehicles). In economic contractions and recessions, corporate jet purchases and fleet expansions are easily deferred or cancelled. Textron lacks the non-discretionary essentiality or entrenched daily habit required of a compounding franchise, as further evidenced by sub-hurdle multi-cycle ROIC of 5-8%.
qualitative.evidence: Textron Inc. operates four primary segments: Textron Aviation (~40% of FY2025 revenue at $5.96B), Bell (~29% at $4.28B), Industrial (~22% at $3.21B), and Textron Systems (~8% at $1.25B). Business jets (Cessna Citation) and specialized vehicles represent classic big-ticket, deferrable cyclical capital purchases rather than essential functional necessities or high-frequency everyday habits. Historical capital efficiency demonstrates persistent vulnerability to cyclicality: GAAP/operating ROIC was 4.4% in 2020, 6.4% in 2021, 6.4% in 2022, 7.6% in 2023, 5.7% in 2024, and 6.4% in 2025 (10-year median ROIC ~9.5%), consistently failing the 12% compounder hurdle across all cycle stages.
